info.name: Incident Management – reporter and assignee flows
info.description:
Complete flows from both sides: the **reporter** (Bob) and the **assignee**. There is no assignee field: an incident is owned by a team, and any member works on it. Here Dan (Database) is the assignee, Alice his team lead, Carol (Platform) the assignee after a hand-over, and Erin (Network) the assignee of a VPN incident.

Each flow creates its own incident, checks what each side may and may not do, then checks every email in Mailpit (exactly which person gets which email) and the history in audit-service. Run a folder, or the whole collection, in order, with the *services-local* environment.

The roles are collection variables (`reporter`, `assignee`, `teamLead`, `platformAssignee`, `networkAssignee`); every write sends a new `Idempotency-Key`.

variable.description: Bob Reporter: no team, reports incidents
Alice Lead: TEAM_LEAD of Database (and responder in Network)
Wait before checking Mailpit (SEV1/SEV2 emails go out within about a second)
Wait before reading a history: it is built from events

item.name: A. Report → acknowledge → resolve → close
item.description: Bob reports a database problem. The Database team (Alice, Dan) owns it; Dan works on it as the assignee, Alice resolves it, Dan closes it. Shows what the reporter may and may not do, and which emails each side gets.

header.description: A new key per request; repeat it to retry safely

request.description: A reporter may set at most SEV2; only the owning team escalates further.

header.description: A new key per request; repeat it to retry safely

request.description: Any active user may report. The category decides the owning team, whose members are emailed. A reporter may set at most SEV2.
The reporter follows their own incidents, newest first.

header.description: A new key per request; repeat it to retry safely

request.description: Title and description may be changed by the reporter or the owning team; no emails.

exec: pm.test("description updated", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().description).to.eql("Pages take 10 s to load; started after the 9:00 deploy"));

request.description: Status, severity and hand-over are for the owning team only.
Dan sees the incidents his team owns.

exec: pm.test("the new incident is OPEN in the queue", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().find(i => i.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("flowAIncident")).status).to.eql("OPEN"));

item.name: Reporter: view the incident with comments

exec: pm.test("both comments, oldest first", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().comments.map(c => c.text)).to.eql(["Looking at the slow queries on the primary", "Also affects the mobile app"]));

request.description: IN_PROGRESS → IN_REVIEW; no emails.

request.description: Resolving, cancelling and reopening need a reason.

header.description: A new key per request; repeat it to retry safely

request.description: IN_REVIEW → RESOLVED. The team and the reporter are emailed, with the resolution.

exec: pm.test("resolutionNote is Missing index rebuilt", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().resolutionNote).to.eql("Missing index rebuilt"));

header.description: A new key per request; repeat it to retry safely

request.description: RESOLVED → CLOSED, final; no emails.

item.name: Reporter: may not comment on a closed incident

header.description: A new key per request; repeat it to retry safely

request.description: Only OPEN, IN_PROGRESS and IN_REVIEW incidents take comments.
Team: new incident and resolved. Reporter: being worked on, and resolved. Review, comments and closing send nothing.

exec: const expected = ["alice@example.com | [SEV2] New incident", "dan@example.com | [SEV2] New incident", "bob@example.com | [SEV2] Your incident is being worked on", "alice@example.com | [SEV2] Resolved", "dan@example.com | [SEV2] Resolved", "bob@example.com | [SEV2] Resolved"].sort();
pm.test("exactly these emails, each once", () => pm.expect(got).to.eql(expected));

request.description: Everything both sides did, oldest first.

exec: pm.test("one entry per change, in order", () => pm.expect(h.map(e => e.action)).to.eql(["INCIDENT_CREATED", "DETAILS_UPDATED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "COMMENT_ADDED", "COMMENT_ADDED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "STATUS_CHANGED"]));
pm.test("resolution recorded", () => pm.expect(h[6].details).to.include({from: "IN_REVIEW", to: "RESOLVED", note: "Missing index rebuilt"}));

item.name: B. Escalation with hand-over to another team
item.description: Dan (Database) finds the cause is in payments: he escalates to SEV1 and hands the incident over to Platform. Carol (Platform) becomes the assignee, de-escalates once it is contained, and closes it.

header.description: A new key per request; repeat it to retry safely

header.description: A new key per request; repeat it to retry safely

request.description: Final.
The escalation emails come from escalation-service; Dan, who escalated, and Carol, who de-escalated, are not emailed about their own change.

exec: const expected = ["alice@example.com | [SEV2] New incident", "dan@example.com | [SEV2] New incident", "bob@example.com | [SEV2] Your incident is being worked on", "carol@example.com | [SEV1] Escalated to you", "alice@example.com | [SEV1] Handed over to Platform", "bob@example.com | [SEV1] Your incident was escalated", "bob@example.com | [SEV1] Your incident is being worked on", "bob@example.com | [SEV2] Your incident was de-escalated", "carol@example.com | [SEV2] Resolved", "bob@example.com | [SEV2] Resolved"].sort();
pm.test("exactly these emails, each once", () => pm.expect(got).to.eql(expected));

pm.test("one entry per change, in order", () => pm.expect(h.map(e => e.action)).to.eql(["INCIDENT_CREATED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "ESCALATED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "DE_ESCALATED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "STATUS_CHANGED"]));

pm.test("hand-over recorded", () => pm.expect(h[2].details).to.include({fromSeverity: "SEV2", toSeverity: "SEV1", fromTeam: pm.variables.get("teamDatabase"), toTeam: pm.variables.get("teamPlatform")}));

pm.test("one entry per change, in order", () => pm.expect(h.map(e => e.action)).to.eql(["INCIDENT_CREATED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "STATUS_CHANGED", "STATUS_CHANGED"]));

exec: const expected = ["alice@example.com | [SEV2] New incident", "dan@example.com | [SEV2] New incident", "alice@example.com | [SEV2] Cancelled", "dan@example.com | [SEV2] Cancelled", "bob@example.com | [SEV2] Cancelled"].sort();
